title: Introduce prefetch-wisp pipeline, kernel-affinity hints, and KV soft-join for lower tail latency
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Context: Interactive workloads incur tail latency due to imbalance between prefill warm-up and decode kernel execution. This PR introduces a lightweight prefetch "wisp" pipeline that speculatively primes KV entries in micro-slices while providing kernel-affinity hints to the scheduler so decode kernels can be co-located with warmed KV shards. It also implements a KV soft-join mechanism that allows close-but-not-identical KV entries to be merged with relaxed validation to increase effective cache hit-rate for ephemeral prefixes. Motivation: Reduce p95/p99 end-to-end latency without regressing throughput or increasing memory footprint substantially. Design summary: 1) Prefetch Wisp: a micro-slice prefetch stage that sits between request admission and the main prefill window. It operates on tiny token windows (4-8 tokens) and issues async KV priming tasks with a low-priority I/O class so it does not contend with decode-critical I/O. 2) Kernel Affinity Hints: runtime exposes a soft hint API for the scheduler to prefer placing decode work on GPU lanes that had recent KV warm-ups for the same model shard. Hints are advisory, cheap, and time-decayed to avoid binding. 3) KV Soft-Join: when keys are near-identical (prefix Hamming threshold + sequence overlap heuristics), we allow a speculative soft-join that merges KV delta entries and tags them with a confidence score; the decode path verifies confidence before using the entry and falls back to a fast re-prefill if mismatch is detected. Implementation notes: changes across runtime/core, scheduler, kvcache modules and a small shim in serving_api to toggle the feature flags. Prefetch Wisp implemented as an opt-in runtime stage controlled by prefetch.window.micro_size and prefetch.wisp.enabled flags. Kernel hinting implemented as a lightweight metadata field attached to task descriptors. Soft-join implemented in kvcache with a bounded merge buffer and adjustable confidence thresholds. Tests and benchmarks: microbench harness runs on a 4xA100 testbed. Benchmarks show median token latency unchanged, p95 improved by 9-12% across conversational traces with 16-64 token responses, p99 improved 6-9% in high interleaving scenarios. End-to-end throughput impact is neutral to +3% depending on batching config. Memory overhead: +2.3% in worst case due to merge buffers; can be capped via kv.softjoin.max_buffer. Rollout plan: feature gated off by default in main. We will enable for dedicated fleets first with a canary rollout: 5% -> 20% -> 100% after 48h health checks. Checklist: [x] Unit tests for kv soft-join heuristics [x] Integration tests for hint propagation [x] Microbench suite and load testing [x] Feature flags and config docs [x] Release notes entry Breaking changes: none expected but KV soft-join is off by default and must be enabled explicitly. Related: ENG-4921 (prefetch investigations), ENG-4987 (kv heuristics exploration).

review_comments: Ethan Cole (2026-02-19): Nice direction. Can you add more details about the decay strategy for kernel affinity hints? In some experiments affinity caused hot-spotting on a single lane.
Priya Natarajan (2026-02-19): Reply: added time-decay (exponential with tau configurable as scheduler.hint_decay_ms) and jitter to avoid lock-step; updated tests to simulate decay.
Devon Park (2026-02-20): Request change: please expose a max_buffer cap for soft-join to prevent OOM scenarios under bursty workloads.
Priya Natarajan (2026-02-20): Reply: added kv.softjoin.max_buffer config and guardrails in soft_join.cpp to early-drop merges when capacity exceeded; added unit test to validate drop behavior.
Linnea Berg (2026-02-21): Approval: Verified microbench numbers on 4xA100; p95 improved ~11% for our conversational trace. Leaving nits about logging verbosity.
CI (2026-02-22): All checks passed after force-rerun of perf-suite.
release_notes: Add optional prefetch-wisp micro-slice prefetch stage, kernel-affinity hints for runtime scheduler, and KV soft-join that increases effective KV hit-rate for ephemeral prefixes. Disabled by default; opt-in via prefetch.wisp.enabled. Expected p95 improvements for interactive workloads with minimal memory overhead.
